entries.disk_gb: ≈23,6 GB (DiT bf16 14,2 + Qwen3VL-8B int8 9,4 + VAE bf16)
entries.time_measured: Sampling ~18 s for 1024²/20 steps (identical in int8 and bf16); ~55-58 s total time per image, almost all of it model load + broker overhead; the model table cites ~40-60 s at 720p+.
entries.quality_notes: Overall winner of the hard-prompt battery (2026-09-21, 18 generations, 4 models, same prompt and seed): 0 text errors on a Spanish sign with an ñ, 5/5 objects and 5/5 price labels correctly assigned, and the only one that truly blends the fox+forest double exposure. Native 2K. bf16 is the default and beats int8 on paired viewing (the int8 weights were removed on 2026-09-21). Inherited QA rule: perceptual A/Bs are judged by eye, never by mean pixel diff.
entries.when_not_to_use: Non-commercial (Qwen Research License). Avoid it for fine anatomy and instruments: it failed the cello portrait (scroll glued to the pegbox, left hand missing) -> use FLUX.2 Klein 9B. Not the best at raw text legibility (Z-Image) or skin realism (MOSS). With very short briefs it may invent an extra arm: use the opt-in --prompt-enhance.
entries.workflow_ref: --model qwen-image-2.1 (opt-in --prompt-enhance for short briefs); 5-slot prompting guide in references/qwen-image-2-1-prompt-guide.md

entries.disk_gb: 11 GB per bf16 checkpoint (distilled and base) + Qwen3VL-4B (size not listed) + shared FLUX.2 VAE
entries.time_measured: ~6-8 s/1MP at 16 steps on the distilled: the fastest arm with quality on the table (RTX 5090). VRAM: not measured.
entries.quality_notes: Perfect Spanish text in the three-way A/B (tie with Qwen and MOSS, ñ included) and a clean product shot with no incoherent micro-text. Ties Qwen on the Artificial Analysis t2i Elo (1043 vs 1042). Skin behind MOSS: the distilled over-sharpens pores; the base checkpoint is visibly more photographic.
entries.when_not_to_use: Realistic skin portrait (use MOSS, or the base + upsampler). Reported strength on anatomy in complex poses. Trained on long LLM captions: it weakens with bare short prompts, and may crop a full-body shot unless you insist on it.

entries.workflow_ref: --model flux3-klein (16 steps cfg 1.0) / --model flux3-klein-base (50 steps cfg 4.0, variant for training LoRA)

entries.model: Z-Image-Turbo (6B S3-DiT destilado, Alibaba Tongyi Lab)
entries.time_measured: ~1-2 s per image (skill table, RTX 5090): the fastest installed option; 8 AuraFlow steps. Disk weight: not measured.
entries.quality_notes: Qwen3-4B encoder; excellent text including Spanish. Best legibility of the battery (uniform high-contrast bold) on the long Spanish sign, and it beat FLUX.2 Klein in the Spanish-text comparison.
entries.when_not_to_use: No image editing (rejects input image). In scenes with many objects and labels it swapped one price and dropped one label. Its text is more signage than editorial.

entries.model: Ideogram 4.0 (9.3B DiT un flujo + encoder Qwen3-VL-8B)
entries.time_measured: ~70 s end-to-end at 1280×720 with the default preset (including the ~29 GB load); ~4x slower than the rest. Presets: quality 48 steps / default 20 / turbo 12.
entries.quality_notes: #1 open-weights on the Artificial Analysis leaderboard (Elo ~1012). 0 text errors in the A/B, best on hands in the hands + small-text test, native 2K, and explicit layout control by bbox with a hex palette.
entries.when_not_to_use: Safety filter trained into the weights: with natural-language prompts it blocks at a high false-positive rate (2 blocks in the hard battery), so you have to feed it the JSON caption (the script generates it with the local LLM; with no LLM, expect blocks). No editing (rejects input image). Non-commercial.
entries.workflow_ref: --model ideogram4 [--preset quality]; the script expands the prompt into a JSON caption with the local LLM automatically

entries.disk_gb: ≈20 GB (DiT bf16 10,2 + int8 encoder 9,75; the bf16 encoder at 19,3 GB does not fit alongside the bf16 DiT)
entries.time_measured: No time measurement in the documentation. Validated recipe: er_sde / simple / 30 steps / cfg 2.5, negative 'plastic skin, waxy skin'.
entries.quality_notes: Won the skin-realism A/B against Qwen 2.1 (sun spots, pores, knit texture versus Qwen's too-clean skin) and obeyed the documentary scene; tie on Spanish text (perfect Ñ) and on simple hands, with an edge on the full-body shot. Commercially safe alternative when Qwen and Ideogram are not an option.
entries.when_not_to_use: t2i only: rejects input image (the experimental edit node is not installed). It lost the product brief: it drifted to a lifestyle scene and invented incoherent micro-text under the correct brand label. Not usable for text-heavy signs.
entries.workflow_ref: --model moss-image --moss-negative "plastic skin, waxy skin"; requires ComfyUI ≥ 0.42 (latent in FLUX.2 format, shared VAE)

entries.quality_notes: Distillation of FLUX.2 Dev (32B) down to 9B: native 4MP, better prompt adherence and anatomy than FLUX.1 Dev despite being smaller. It clearly won the cello portrait (correct instrument anatomy and both hands) where Qwen failed.
entries.when_not_to_use: Exact on-screen text: in the A/B it mutated 'DEL'→'DE' and 'ESPECIALIDAD'→'ESPECIALDAD'. In i2i the input has to be reduced to ~1-2 MP (long side 1536 px) or sampling goes from seconds to minutes.

entries.disk_gb: ≈23,6 GB (DiT bf16 14,2 + Qwen3VL-8B int8 9,4 + VAE bf16)
entries.time_measured: Sampling ~18 s for 1024²/20 steps; ~55-58 s total time per image (model load + broker overhead).
entries.quality_notes: The only multi-reference editor installed (up to 16 references on the node) and the only one with real RGBA: verified alpha (21,9 % of pixels fully transparent), clean edge and semi-transparent contact shadow inside the alpha channel itself. Background swap with identity 8,5/10; two people in the same scene 8/10 without crossing identities; recomposing the cat to the window with rim-light and shadow integration 8/10.
entries.when_not_to_use: The prompt text overrides the pixels: if it contradicts the photo, it invents what was asked. It swapped who sits on which side with two references (FLUX 3 Klein won that). No commercial license. Region/mask edits are documented but still not wired into the script.
entries.workflow_ref: --model qwen-image-2.1 --image [--image2 …]; pattern 'define each Figure N up front and in the same upload order' (prompting guide §6)

entries.disk_gb: 11 GB per checkpoint + Qwen3VL-4B; references are scaled to 1 MP in the graph (VRAM: not measured)
entries.time_measured: 16 steps in edit mode: ties Qwen on the background swap with identity while being ~4-8x faster.
entries.quality_notes: Co-default for editing with Qwen: it honored the left/right position of the two references and rendered credible hands on the table where Qwen swapped the seated people; in the background swap it tied while preserving face, hair and t-shirt pattern.
entries.when_not_to_use: Not pixel-exact preservation: with a prompt that contradicts the photo both models invent (no installed editor is truly pixel-preserving). In editing you must pin guidance to 1.0 on both checkpoints: the t2i defaults are wrong. RGBA and product-brief edits remain Qwen's.

entries.time_measured: 3-5 s with the input at ~1 MP; with a 3072×4096 phone photo the same job goes from seconds to many minutes.
entries.quality_notes: Native editing via a ReferenceLatent chain (one VAE encode and one node per reference, chained, no ImageStitch); cfg 4.0 and denoise 0.75 by default, 0.60 for subtle changes, 0.90 for a strong reimagine. Best anatomical and instrument detail of the battery.
entries.when_not_to_use: Not for exact text (it mutates words). Do not assign contradictory roles to two references, and do not keep the original photo at full size. Review and reduce the input image before editing.
entries.workflow_ref: --model flux2-klein-9b --image [--image2] (double reference by chaining, not by stitching)

entries.disk_gb: ≈23,3 GB (DiT 23 + VAE 0,32) + clip_l and t5xxl (sizes not listed)
entries.quality_notes: Character consistency via Kontext: the recommended route for generating the reference-frame set when recurring identity across clips is what matters.
entries.when_not_to_use: On-screen text and native resolution below FLUX.2 Klein / Qwen 2.1. For many references or transparent output you have to go to Qwen 2.1 or FLUX 3 Klein. No dated A/B of its own.

entries.model: MiniMax H3 Still (nodos Fizgig sobre los pesos de vídeo H3)
entries.disk_gb: 0,78 GB (turbo LoRA) — reuses the already installed H3 video weights: zero extra downloads (VRAM: not measured)
entries.time_measured: 1,3 MP ~110-118 s; 2,5 MP ~128-134 s per image (warm, turbo 20 steps).
entries.quality_notes: The second serious editor of the A/B against Qwen: it wins or ties on editing with identity (near-identical t-shirt pattern) and on multi-reference with two identities without crossing, plus a richer pub scene with natural laughter; it copies dense fur better than Qwen; perfect Spanish text, tie included (Ñ).
entries.when_not_to_use: It does not obey negative expression clauses: 'closed jaw, no teeth, no paw on the shoulder' failed 2/2 runs, so changing a keyframe's expression has to be solved with a re-roll. Its edge on fine t2i is unconfirmed (it was tested at 1,3 MP and performs from 3 MP up). Still not wired as a flag in the image script.
entries.workflow_ref: Its own API wiring (H3 image node + Fizgig still node, refs as dotted keys ref_images.ref_image_N; turbo LoRA at strength 0,38); it does not accept an input image through the image script

entries.model: Upsampler de prompt de BFL para FLUX 3 (Qwen3.5-9B, opt-in --upsample)
entries.disk_gb: 9,75 GB (int8_convrot weight in the ComfyUI models folder); it does not scale pixels, it rewrites the prompt (VRAM: not measured)
entries.time_measured: No time measurement; the upsampler load happens once per broker batch.
entries.quality_notes: ON wins 4 clear victories and 1 narrow one on detailed briefs because it pins the brief down where pure Klein drifts: skin with natural irregularities instead of over-carved uniform blotches, a clean studio product shot (OFF drifted to a lifestyle kitchen), full-body shot respected and a tea stall that really serves. The sign text came out 3/3 perfect on both branches. Watch the flag's A/Bs: there was a silent wiring failure, always check that the text-generation node is in the graph.
entries.when_not_to_use: Short ambient prompts: OFF won clearly (richer landscape but stick legs, an odd smile and clipped light). It only applies to t2i with flux3-klein. Skip it when exact text legibility matters more than layout, and careful: it can invent props with pseudo-text (newspapers, signs).

entries.model: Refiner latent Open-H3-Regenerate-2K + latent upscaler 3D conv
entries.disk_gb: ≈0,69 GB for the 3D conv bf16 latent upscaler + regenerate 2K LoRA (size not listed); VRAM rules over time: the refine runs at the target resolution
entries.time_measured: Measured over video frames, not over a still image: 5 s @1080p 178 s; 5 s @2560×1440 293 s; 15 s @2K OOM (split into 5 s chunks). Without the quantized-attention patch: 9,4 s @2K ~15 min clean. Time on a still image: not measured.
entries.quality_notes: A real and large detail gain (microphone, leather) but with identity drift in the first QA: pink nose→black nose, duller eye, reshaped paw, warmer whites. σ NOTE (identity > texture): the official σ0.909 curve buys maximum detail by regenerating micro-attributes (nose color, iris, finger shape), and in wide shots with several subjects it rewrites species and anatomy; the chroma anchor (Y from the refined + Cb/Cr from the scaled draft, zero cost) fixes color, never shape. Adopted criterion: lower σ —less new detail— rather than accept identity changes; σ0.667 preserves identity, and σ0.909 + chroma anchor is only validated on a single-subject close-up. QA always by eye covering ALL subjects, hands and background, not just the main face. When chaining the sampler with SchedulerCustom: the scaled latent comes in clean because the sampler already blends it at sigmas[0]; pre-noising it leaves ~1 % of the signal and the refine hallucinates a different scene.
entries.when_not_to_use: Do not use by default on multi-subject shots, wide shots or footage with critical identity without first running a σ A/B on the most crowded shot. Native 4K is off the table (refine at 2K and scale afterwards). Avoid the quantized-attention patch on clips >5 s: it degrades with length and produces uniform garbage with no error.
entries.workflow_ref: Refine at the target resolution with a short per-shot prompt (never the generation prompt) + chroma anchor; σ0.667 prompt as fallback for identity-obsessive shots
